extracted.intended_audience: senior biomedical researchers (faculty) considering application to the HHMI Investigator Program
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and eligibility/selection criteria for applying to the Howard Hughes Medical Institute (HHMI) Investigator Program, describing who may apply, what materials to submit, and the qualities HHMI looks for in investigators. Focused on selecting outstanding individual scientists rather than specific projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection emphasis: people not projects
rubrics_metrics.description: HHMI supports people, rather than projects, because it’s individual scientists who break barriers to advance knowledge. HHMI selects people, not projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications should present the investigator — their record, potential, and overall research program — rather than treating the application as a narrowly defined, time-limited project proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrated scientific discovery and impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators are widely known for their scientific discoveries, their innovation, and their success in pushing the bounds of knowledge in biomedical research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should document a record of important discoveries and high-impact contributions to their field; examples include major published findings and evidence of advancing understanding in cells, brain, immune system, organ development, or disease mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation and method/tool development
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators develop new tools and methods that make it possible to ask previously unapproachable questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight development of novel techniques, technologies, or conceptual approaches that enabled new lines of inquiry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Willingness to take intellectual risk
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators ask tough questions in science, even at the risk of failure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate a track record or planned research agenda that pursues high‑risk/high‑reward questions rather than only safe, incremental work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment to mentoring and training
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators are committed to mentoring and training the next generation of scientists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include evidence of mentorship, training activities, leadership roles, and contributions to developing students, postdocs, and junior colleagues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: degree requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must hold a PhD and/or MD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a baseline eligibility requirement for applicants to the competition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: institutional/host location
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must plan to perform research at one of over 200 eligible U.S. institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm that the intended host institution is on the list of eligible institutions for the competition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: institutional commitment/position
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must hold a position that represents substantial commitment by their institution, such as a tenure-track faculty position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications should indicate a concurrent appointment or other formal commitment by the host institution that supports the investigator’s long-term research activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: peer-reviewed funding track record
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must have a track record of peer-reviewed funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document past success securing competitive, peer-reviewed grants or equivalent external support as evidence of research independence and recognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experience/years-since-training requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Each competition defines a required length of post-training, professional experience prior to the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the specific Program Announcement for the precise experience window for the current competition year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disciplinary scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Each competition defines the breadth of scientific disciplines to be considered; however, most competitions are open to most biological and biomedical disciplines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check the Program Announcement to confirm whether your discipline is included in the current competition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application materials: highlighted publications and summary
rubrics_metrics.description: Application requirements include five highlighted research articles and a summary of your major research contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select up to five publications that best represent your contributions; provide concise summaries explaining the significance of each and how they reflect your overall scientific impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application materials: program description focused on ongoing/planned research
rubrics_metrics.description: Application requires a program description focused on your ongoing and planned research program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe the investigator’s overall research agenda and future directions rather than a narrowly bounded project plan; emphasize continuity, potential for discovery, and how HHMI support would accelerate the program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application process: direct application, no nomination limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants apply directly; there is no nomination process and no limit on the number of applications from a single institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure compliance with submission procedures; institutions need not endorse or limit applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection process: peer assessment and HHMI leadership decision
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection of investigators is made by HHMI scientific leadership and is based on assessment by a panel of distinguished scientists, including members of HHMI advisory boards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect review by external panels; present materials that clearly convey your scientific stature, originality, and potential for continued high-impact work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment term and renewal
rubrics_metrics.description: The HHMI investigator appointment has a seven-year renewable term. Renewal decisions are made by HHMI scientific leadership, based on assessment by a panel of distinguished scientists, including members of HHMI advisory boards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigators should be prepared for periodic performance evaluation toward renewal and to demonstrate continued excellence and progress over the appointment term.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employment and host-institution agreement requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators are employees of HHMI and appointments involve a collaborative agreement with the investigator’s host institution, where the researcher holds a concurrent appointment and the research is performed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must coordinate with their host institution to establish the necessary collaborative agreement and concurrent appointment arrangements if selected.
